newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens flat on quiet overseas session.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens flat on quiet overseas session.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened flat at C$1.3864 (US$0.7212) in light trading after a quiet overnight session in overseas trading, dealers said. * They said the release of inflation data in the United States and Canada yesterday meant interest rates in both countries would remain unchanged until the middle of the third quarter, confining the Canada dollar to a narrow range.

"I think we've reverted to range trading with little sign that the Canada dollar is about to stray far from C$1.3870 (US$0.7209)," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser at CIBC-Wood Gundy.
But Farrill cautioned that there could be "interesting trading activity" if the Canada dollar broke through technical support at C$1.3885 (US$0.7202).

With little U.S. economic data due to be released today, analysts said markets continued to discount the possibility that the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise interest rates at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2.
The consensus is that the U.S. economy is moving along at a reasonable pace with little inflationary pressure appearing on the horizon.

"We didn't see a Fed move in May and, with this recent data out yesterday, it doesn't look like we'll see one in July. Even a probability of a move in August is diminishing," said Paul Ferley, assistant chief economist with the Bank of Montreal.
Ferley said he was surprised that the Canadian dollar failed to rally on the soft inflation data. "It should have been more supportive of the Canadian dollar," Ferley said.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar dipped to 81.54 from Tuesday's 81.73 and rose to 1.2450 marks from Tuesday's 1.2480 marks.
